subject: On-prem control plane — split-admin model, SCIM delta plan, and emergency breakglass
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: James Martin <j.martin@helios.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Sep 2025 08:32:00 -0700
Subject: On-prem control plane — split-admin model, SCIM delta plan, and emergency breakglass

James / Helios security team —

Thanks again for the walk-through yesterday. Per our call, we're putting together the access model and a lightweight reconciliation runbook for the private control plane you will host in your VPC. The two things we want to align on before the validation run are:

- operational model for operator vs service accounts (who can act as an operator, who can only provision workloads)
- SCIM reconciliation strategy for contractor accounts and group membership deltas
- emergency breakglass (how we regain access if federation is down)

Attached are the draft artifacts: a split-admin matrix (privcp_split_admin_matrix.xlsx) and a first-pass SCIM delta script (scim_delta_script_v1.patch). High level proposals below — please confirm what works for Helios: 

1) Split-admin model
   - Operators: short-lived operator roles mapped from SAML Role attribute; no long-lived console passwords.
   - Service accounts: managed via SCIM + bound to a service identity; recommended to use push-based SCIM provisioning for service accounts.
   - Breakglass: a single HSM-protected breakglass key with MFA and documented E2E playbook (attached).

2) SCIM reconciliation
   - Primary mode: delta recon (incremental) once/hour, push from Helios IdP to our SCIM endpoint.
   - Reconciliation behavior: group merges only; do not auto-delete if membership disappears until a 24h grace window passes.

3) Fallbacks and telemetry
   - If SAML federation fails, operator access should be possible via breakglass with strict MFA + audit.
   - All operator actions will be logged to an append-only audit stream we ship to your SIEM. Retention and export policy TBD.

Can you confirm: (a) IdP team has access to metadata export; (b) Helios can run the SCIM push through a service account with scoped token; (c) breakglass approach is acceptable?

Next step: schedule a validation run next week if we have IdP metadata by Monday.

Thanks,
Olga
OLGA PETROV
Security & Integrations Lead
Redwood Inference
Attachments: privcp_split_admin_matrix.xlsx (xlsx), scim_delta_script_v1.patch (patch), emergency-breakglass-playbook.pdf (pdf)

From: James Martin <j.martin@helios.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: security@helios.com, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Sep 2025 09:15:00 -0400
Subject: Re: On-prem control plane — split-admin model, SCIM delta plan, and emergency breakglass

Olga —

Thanks for the clear summary and the attachments. A few quick clarifications from Helios IdP/security: 

- Contractors: we have a separate SCIM group path for contractors with shorter TTLs and automated expiration. Can your delta logic respect TTL-based tombstoning so we don't prematurely orphan accounts?
- Service accounts: we prefer short-lived STS-style credentials for anything that needs AWS access; for Redwood service identities that don't need cloud APIs, we can provision via SCIM.
- Breakglass: we're comfortable with an HSM-backed key, but we'd like the playbook to require a 2-person approval (1 Helios admin + 1 Redwood). Can that be enforced in the runbook?

We will upload IdP metadata and a SCIM service account by Monday. Also sending this to our SOC distribution (security@helios.com) for visibility.

James Martin
Head of Cloud Security, Helios Financial

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: James Martin <j.martin@helios.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Sep 2025 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: On-prem control plane — split-admin model, SCIM delta plan, and emergency breakglass

James —

Great questions. Short answers and technical notes below; I've also left inline comments in scim_delta_script_v1.patch.

- Contractor TTLs: agree — we'll add TTL-aware tombstone handling. Proposal: SCIM patch will mark contractor accounts with "expires_at" and we will skip hard-deletes until a separate reconciliation pass confirms >24h beyond expires_at. I added a flag `--respect-ttl` in the patch.

- STS-style creds: for any operation requiring cloud-level API access you should use short-lived STS tokens. For pure control-plane operations (e.g., model pinning, routing policy updates) we recommend binding a Redwood service identity to a SCIM-provisioned app account and using short-lived OAuth tokens issued by our token service.

- Breakglass 2-person approval: we can implement a mandatory approval workflow in the playbook. Practically: the breakglass workflow will require one escalation token from Helios (signed by your admin) and one sign-off from a Redwood on-call (we'll provide an M-of-N signing endpoint). All steps are logged and emitted to your SIEM.

Operational checklist I'm proposing (high level):
1) Exchange SAML metadata + IDP contact (you by Mon)
2) Provision SCIM service account with scope `scim:write:users,scim:read:groups`
3) Run a dry-run reconciliation against a snapshot environment (no deletes)
4) Confirm audit export to your SIEM and retention policy
5) Schedule a cutover window and runbook walk-through

I'll push a tiny update to the patch (TTL handling) and ping here when done.

- Dev
Dev Patel
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: James Martin <j.martin@helios.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Sep 2025 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: On-prem control plane — split-admin model, SCIM delta plan, and emergency breakglass

James / team —

Thanks — from an operational readiness perspective, a couple of additions to Dev's checklist: 

- Canary plan: we'll run reconciliation against a 1% subset (test accounts) first, monitor audit events for 48h, then increase to 10% before full cutover.
- Rollback criteria: if >0.5% of active operator accounts are unexpectedly changed during the 10% run, we rollback and pause automation.
- Audit retention: default 365 days for operator audit events; longer retention can be exported on demand.
- Communication matrix: Helios will own the first-level on-call during your cutover window; Redwood will provide a dedicated SE for the runbook.

I've attached the emergency-breakglass-playbook.pdf which includes the two-person approval template and play-by-play. Can we lock a 60-minute validation slot on Wed 24 Sep? I'll send a calendar invite once James confirms his IdP team can provide metadata by Mon.

Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: emergency-breakglass-playbook.pdf (pdf)

From: James Martin <j.martin@helios.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, security@helios.com
Date: Thu, 18 Sep 2025 14:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: On-prem control plane — split-admin model, SCIM delta plan, and emergency breakglass

Marissa / Olga / Dev —

All good on our end. Helios IdP team will upload metadata and create the SCIM service account by Monday morning; they will add TTLs to contractor entries. We confirm the two-person breakglass approach (Helios + Redwood).

Wed 24 Sep 2025 14:00 ET for a 60-minute validation works for us — please send invite. We'll be prepared to run the dry reconcile against test subset during that time.

Thanks,
James
Head of Cloud Security, Helios Financial
